tools.name: developerknowledge_answer_query
tools.description:
Use answer_query to get a grounded answer to a query about Google developer products. This tool has limited quota. This tool will synthesize information from the corpus to generate an answer to the query. answer_query grounds answers using the same corpus as search_documents. 
This tool returns the generated answer_text and a list of document names (references) used to generate the answer. Use get_documents with the document names to fetch the entire document content if needed.

If you get a 429 out of quota error, use search_documents instead.

references.description: Output only. The resource names of the documents used to generate the answer.

tools.name: developerknowledge_get_documents
tools.description: Use this tool to retrieve the full content of a single document or up to 20 documents in a single call. The document names should be obtained from the `parent` field of results from a call to the `search_documents` tool. Set the `names` parameter to a list of document names.

names.description: Required. The names of the documents to retrieve, as returned by search_documents. A maximum of 20 documents can be retrieved in one call. The documents are returned in the same order as the `names` in the request. Format: `documents/{uri_without_scheme}` Example: `documents/docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/creating-buckets`

Document.description: A Document represents a piece of content from the Developer Knowledge corpus.

content.description: Output only. The content of the document in Markdown format.

description.description: Output only. A description of the document.

name.description: Identifier. The resource name of the document. Format: `documents/{uri_without_scheme}` Example: `documents/docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/creating-buckets`

title.description: Output only. The title of the document.

uri.description: Output only. The URI of the content, such as `https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/creating-buckets`.

tools.name: developerknowledge_search_documents
tools.description:
Use this tool to find documentation about Google developer products. The documents contain official APIs, code snippets, release notes, best practices, guides, debugging info, and more. It covers the following products and domains:


* ADK: adk.dev

* Android: developer.android.com

* Apigee: docs.apigee.com

* Chrome: developer.chrome.com

* Dart: dart.dev

* Firebase: firebase.google.com

* Flutter: docs.flutter.dev

* Fuchsia: fuchsia.dev

* Gemini CLI: geminicli.com

* Go: go.dev

* Google AI: ai.google.dev

* Google Antigravity: antigravity.google

* Google Cloud: cloud.google.com & docs.cloud.google.com

* Google Developers, Ads, Search, Google Maps, Youtube: developers.google.com

* Google Home: developers.home.google.com

* Google Maps Platform: mapsplatform.google.com

* TensorFlow: www.tensorflow.org

* Web: web.dev


This tool returns chunks of text, names, and URLs for matching documents. If the returned chunks are not detailed enough to answer the user's question, use `get_documents` with the `parent` from this tool's output to retrieve the full document content.

query.description: Required. The raw query string provided by the user, such as "How to create a Cloud Storage bucket?".

inputSchema.description: Request schema for search_documents. Use the query field to search for related Google developer documentation.

results.description: The search results for the given query. Each Document in this list contains a snippet of content relevant to the search query. Use the DocumentChunk.name field of each result with get_documents to retrieve the full document content.

DocumentChunk.description: A DocumentChunk represents a piece of content from a Document in the DeveloperKnowledge corpus. To fetch the entire document content, pass the `parent` to get_document or batch_get_documents.

content.description: Output only. The content of the document chunk.

id.description: Output only. The ID of this chunk within the document. The chunk ID is unique within a document, but not globally unique across documents. The chunk ID is not stable and may change over time.

parent.description: Output only. The resource name of the document this chunk is from. Format: `documents/{uri_without_scheme}` Example: `documents/docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/creating-buckets`

tools.name: firebase_create_android_sha
tools.description: Use this to add the specified SHA certificate hash to the specified Firebase Android App.

app_id.description: The Android app ID to add the SHA certificate to.

sha_hash.description: The SHA certificate hash to add (SHA-1 or SHA-256).

annotations.title: Add SHA Certificate to Android App

tools.name: firebase_create_app
tools.description: Use this to create a new Firebase App in the currently active Firebase Project. Firebase Apps can be iOS, Android, or Web.

display_name.description: The user-friendly display name for your app. If not provided, a default name may be generated.

platform.description: The platform for which to create an app.

android_config.description: Configuration for Android apps. Required if platform is 'android'.

package_name.description: The package name for your Android app (e.g., com.example.myapp).

ios_config.description: Configuration for iOS apps. Required if platform is 'ios'.

bundle_id.description: The bundle ID for your iOS app (e.g., com.example.myapp).

app_store_id.description: The App Store ID for your iOS app.

tools.name: firebase_create_project
tools.description: Use this to create a new Firebase Project.

project_id.description: The project ID to create or use.

display_name.description: The user-friendly display name for the project.

tools.name: firebase_deploy
tools.description: Deploy resources to your Firebase project, based on the contents of firebase.json.

only.description: Comma-separated list of services to deploy. Valid targets are: database, storage, firestore, functions, hosting, remoteconfig, extensions, dataconnect, apphosting, auth.

tools.name: firebase_deploy_status
tools.description: Check the status of a background deployment job using its Job ID.

jobId.description: The Job ID returned by the deploy tool

tools.name: firebase_get_environment
tools.description: Use this to retrieve the current Firebase **environment** configuration for the Firebase CLI and Firebase MCP server, including current authenticated user, project directory, active Firebase Project, and more. All tools require the user to be authenticated, but not all information is required for all tools. Pay attention to the tool requirements for which pieces of information are required.

tools.name: firebase_get_project
tools.description: Use this to retrieve information about the currently active Firebase Project.

tools.name: firebase_get_sdk_config
tools.description: Use this to retrieve the Firebase configuration information for a Firebase App. You must specify EITHER a platform OR the Firebase App ID for a Firebase App registered in the currently active Firebase Project.

platform.description: The platform for which you want config. One of 'platform' or 'app_id' must be provided.

app_id.description: The specific app ID to fetch. One of 'platform' or 'app_id' must be provided.

tools.name: firebase_get_security_rules
tools.description: Use this to retrieve the security rules for a specified Firebase service. If there are multiple instances of that service in the product, the rules for the default instance are returned.

type.description: The service to get rules for.

tools.name: firebase_init
tools.description: Use this to initialize selected Firebase services in the workspace (Cloud Firestore database, Firebase SQL Connect, Firebase Realtime Database, Firebase AI Logic). All services are optional; specify only the products you want to set up. You can initialize new features into an existing project directory, but re-initializing an existing feature may overwrite configuration. To deploy the initialized features, run the `firebase deploy` command after `firebase_init` tool.

database.description: Provide this object to initialize Firebase Realtime Database in this project directory.

rules_filename.description: The file to use for Realtime Database Security Rules.

rules.description: The security rules to use for Realtime Database Security Rules.

firestore.description: Provide this object to initialize Cloud Firestore in this project directory.

database_id.description: The database ID to use for Firestore.

location_id.description: The GCP region ID to set up the Firestore database.

rules_filename.description: The file to use for Firestore Security Rules.

rules.description: The security rules to use for Firestore Security Rules. Default to open rules that expire in 30 days.

dataconnect.description:
Provide this object to initialize Firebase SQL Connect with Cloud SQL Postgres in this project directory.
It installs SQL Connect Generated SDKs in all detected apps in the folder.

service_id.description: The Firebase SQL Connect service ID to initialize. Default to match the current folder name.

location_id.description: The GCP region ID to set up the Firebase SQL Connect service.

cloudsql_instance_id.description:
The GCP Cloud SQL instance ID to use in the Firebase SQL Connect service. By default, use <serviceId>-fdc. 
Set `provision_cloudsql` to true to start Cloud SQL provisioning.

cloudsql_database.description: The Postgres database ID to use in the Firebase SQL Connect service.

provision_cloudsql.description:
If true, provision the Cloud SQL instance if `cloudsql_instance_id` does not exist already. 
The first Cloud SQL instance in the project will use the SQL Connect no-cost trial. See its terms of service: https://firebase.google.com/pricing.

storage.description: Provide this object to initialize Firebase Storage in this project directory.

rules_filename.description: The file to use for Firebase Storage Security Rules.

rules.description: The security rules to use for Firebase Storage Security Rules. Default to closed rules that deny all access.

ailogic.description: Enable Firebase AI Logic feature for existing app

app_id.description: Firebase app ID (format: 1:PROJECT_NUMBER:PLATFORM:APP_ID). Must be an existing app in your Firebase project.

hosting.description: Provide this object to initialize Firebase Hosting in this project directory.

site_id.description: The ID of the hosting site to configure. If omitted and there is a default hosting site, that will be used.

public_directory.description: The directory containing public files that will be served. If using a build tool, this likely should be the output directory of that tool.

auth.description: Provide this object to initialize Firebase Authentication.

oAuthBrandDisplayName.description: The display name for the OAuth brand.

supportEmail.description: The support email for the OAuth brand.

tools.name: firebase_list_apps
tools.description: Use this to retrieve a list of the Firebase Apps registered in the currently active Firebase project. Firebase Apps can be iOS, Android, or Web.

platform.description: the specific platform to list (omit to list all platforms)

tools.name: firebase_list_projects
tools.description: Use this to retrieve a list of Firebase Projects that the signed-in user has access to.

page_size.description: the number of projects to list per page (defaults to 1000)

page_token.description: the page token to start listing from

tools.name: firebase_login
tools.description: Use this to sign the user into the Firebase CLI and Firebase MCP server. This requires a Google Account, and sign in is required to create and work with Firebase Projects.

authCode.description: The authorization code from the login flow

tools.name: firebase_logout
tools.description: Use this to sign the user out of the Firebase CLI and Firebase MCP server.

email.description: The email of the account to log out. If not provided, all accounts will be logged out.

tools.name: firebase_read_resources
tools.description: Use this to read the contents of `firebase://` resources or list available resources

uris.description: list of resource uris to read. each must start with `firebase://` prefix. omit to list all available resources

tools.name: firebase_update_environment
tools.description: Use this to update environment config for the Firebase CLI and Firebase MCP server, such as project directory, active project, active user account, accept terms of service, and more. Use `firebase_get_environment` to see the currently configured environment.

project_dir.description: Change the current project directory - this should be a directory that has a `firebase.json` file (or will have one).

active_project.description: Change the active project for the current project directory. Should be a Firebase project ID or configured project alias.

active_user_account.description: The email address of the signed-in user to authenticate as when interacting with the current project directory.
